    Portal node

    A Portal defines a global route that can fire regardless of which UI node is active. It has no Enter port. The navigation service checks matching Portals before it checks outputs on the active UI node.

    Use a Portal for truly global controls such as a persistent Home button, a system overlay, or an application-wide signal. If a Portal and the active UI use the same event address, the Portal wins.

    Options and ports

    Setting Description
    Display Name Node title in the graph
    Node Description Authoring note
    Condition Kind UI Button, Signal, or Toggle
    Category / Key Address from the matching Button or Signal catalog
    Toggle Value Value that activates a Toggle Portal
    History Push, Replace, or Back
    Force Transition Required output to one UI or Action chain

    When the Force Transition chain reaches another screen, Push stores the previous screen in Back history and Replace changes screens without modifying history. Back runs the chain's Actions, then requests history navigation instead of entering its connected screen. A terminal Action chain has no screen transition, so Push or Replace does not change history.

    Portal conditions must be unique by event kind, address, and Toggle value. The output must resolve to exactly one valid UI or Action target, even when Pivot nodes are used between them.

    Caution

    Keep Portal addresses narrow. A broad global route can make a local UI output appear unresponsive because the global match is evaluated first.
